incident: A File Of 31,400 Patient Rows Is Public
description: Since 06:40 a paste site has carried a file headed carilion_swva_patients_2026: names, dates of birth, addresses, the last four of a Social Security number, a clinic code. Nobody has established whether it is genuine, whether it is the whole of what was taken, or whether it is even from this breach. Every other decision this phase is sized off that answer, and 31,400 people cannot find out whether they are in it.

incident: A Synthetic Video Of The Liaison Is Circulating
description: A clip of the Governor's SW Virginia Liaison saying the outage was 'an internal decision to protect data' is on every regional feed. She never said it. It is good, and two county officials have already shared it believing it. Until someone establishes that it is synthetic and says so in a form a county can cite, every official statement this phase is read against it.

incident: The Notification Went Out; The Not-Affected Majority Just Got Scared
description: The file is verified and the letters are reaching 31,400 patients. But the notification — and the coverage it triggers — reaches far beyond them. The three clinics' catchment is fifteen thousand families, and every parent now thinks their child's records are in it. The question is what the clinics and the health office say to the people who are not in the file but who are the ones still coming to care, and how the eight in ten whose data is safe are told.

incident: The File Is Confirmed; The Letters Were Never Sent
description: The file is verified — genuine, 31,400 records, exactly the fields claimed. And then nothing was sent. The notification was the one thing only the clinics could do and it did not happen; the people in the file are hearing about it from a paste site and a rumor. The records line and the letter are still unmade, and the scammers are already using the file's own fields to call households.

incident: A Second File, With Billing And Insurance IDs, Lands On The Same Paste Site
description: The first file was verified — and verified honestly. But it was only the first cut, and the assessment stopped at confirmed instead of how far it went. A second file with billing and insurance IDs for the same 31,400 plus 15,600 more is now on the site. The notification being written for 31,400 is wrong by half, and the fraud sites have richer data than the clinics have confirmed.
